questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Beginners must apply concrete security defaults to container specs, learn how policies gate PRs, and validate locally and in CI.

## Key Concepts
- Kubernetes securityContext fields
- Kyverno policy syntax and testing
- CI gate integration in GitHub Actions

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: require-sec-context
spec:
  validationFailureAction: enforce
  rules:
  - name: require-sec-context
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: ["Deployment","StatefulSet","DaemonSet","Job","CronJob"]
    validate:
      message: "Containers must run as non-root with readOnlyRootFilesystem and drop ALL capabilities"
      pattern:
        spec:
          template:
            spec:
              containers:
              - securityContext:
                  runAsNonRoot: true
                  readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
                  capabilities:
                    drop: ["ALL"]
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you adapt this policy for InitContainers? 
- How would you measure policy coverage over time (e.g., CI reports, dashboards)?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

In production Kubernetes environments, ensuring supply-chain security for Helm-based deployments is critical. This question evaluates your ability to integrate multiple security tools—Helm templating, SBOM generation, and image signature verification—into a cohesive CI gate. It tests practical knowledge of enforcing provenance and attestations before code merges.

## Key Concepts

- **Helm templating and values extraction**: Rendering charts to discover all container images referenced in deployments
- **SBOM generation**: Using Syft to create a CycloneDX SBOM that catalogs all dependencies and artifacts
- **Image signing verification**: Using cosign to validate container image signatures against a public key stored in the repository
- **CI gate integration**: Implementing fail-fast behavior in GitHub Actions to block unsigned images and missing attestations

## Code Example

```yaml
# Minimal GitHub Actions workflow for Helm image signing enforcement
name: Helm Image Security Gate

on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]

jobs:
  helm-security:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Install cosign
        uses: sigstore/cosign-installer@v3

      - name: Install Helm and Syft
        run: |
          curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/helm/helm/main/scripts/get-helm-3 | bash
          curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anchore/syft/main/install.sh | sh

      - name: Render Helm templates
        run: helm template my-app ./chart --values values.yaml --output-dir ./rendered

      - name: Extract image references
        run: |
          grep -rh 'image:' ./rendered | awk '{print $2}' > images.txt

      - name: Generate SBOM with Syft
        run: |
          syft $(cat images.txt) -o cyclonedx-json > sbom.json

      - name: Verify image signatures with cosign
        run: |
          COSIGN_PUBLIC_KEY=cosign.pub
          for IMAGE in $(cat images.txt); do
            cosign verify --key $COSIGN_PUBLIC_KEY $IMAGE || exit 1
          done
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Real-world multi-tenant data platforms require strong admission control to enforce image provenance and host security postures across clouds. Gatekeeper with Rego enables centralized policy with testable manifests.

## Key Concepts
- Open Policy Agent Gatekeeper
- ConstraintTemplate and Constraint objects
- Image provenance: registry, non-latest, digest
- Pod hardening: resources, securityContext, privilegeEscalation
- Namespace labeling and admission scope
- CI validation: conftest, gatekeeper audit, sample manifests

## Code Example
```yaml
# ConstraintTemplate (ImageProvenanceAndSecurity)
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: imageprovenance
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: ImageProvenanceConstraint
  targets:
    - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
      rego: |
        package imageprovenance
        violation[{"msg": msg}] {
          some i
          container := input.review.object.spec.template.spec.containers[i]
          image := container.image
          startswith(image, "registry.example.com/")
          not endswith(image, ":latest")
          some digest := input.review.object.spec.template.spec.containers[i].imageDigest
          msg := "image must be from registry.example.com with digest"
        }
```
```yaml
# Constraint (ImageProvenanceConstraint)
apiVersion: constraints.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ImageProvenanceConstraint
metadata:
  name: require-provenance
spec:
  enforcementAction: deny
```

```yaml
# Failing manifest: unsigned or latest, missing resources
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: data-processor
  namespace: data
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: proc
        image: registry.example.com/data/processor:latest
        imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
```

```yaml
# Passing manifest: compliant image, resources, and securityContext
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: data-processor
  namespace: data
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: proc
        image: registry.example.com/data/processor@sha256:abcdef...
        resources:
          requests:
            cpu: "100m"
            memory: "128Mi"
          limits:
            cpu: "500m"
            memory: "512Mi"
        securityContext:
          runAsNonRoot: true
          allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
          readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test policy changes locally before applying to cluster?
- How would you roll out a breaking policy change across multiple namespaces without downtime?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

This question evaluates expertise in policy-as-code across multi-cloud, multi-tenant ML infrastructure. It combines security hardening (image signing, secret management), resource governance (GPU quotas, container limits), network segmentation (default-deny policies), and operational reliability (canary deployments with SLO validation)—all critical for enterprise-grade ML platforms.

## Key Concepts

- **Policy Engines**: Kyverno and OPA Gatekeeper provide declarative, Kubernetes-native admission control
- **Image Signing**: Cosign ensures container image integrity and provenance verification
- **Secret Management**: ExternalSecret/SecretStore enables secure, dynamic secret injection from external stores
- **Resource Quotas**: ResourceQuota and LimitRange enforce compute, memory, and GPU allocation per tenant
- **Network Policies**: Namespace-scoped default-deny with per-tenant allow rules implements zero-trust networking
- **Canary/SLO Integration**: Prometheus metrics validate deployment health before traffic shifting
- **CI Integration**: Automated policy testing and manifest validation ensure consistent enforcement

## Code Example

```yaml
# Kyverno policy: require Cosign-signed images from approved registries
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: require-signed-images
spec:
  validationFailureAction: Enforce
  rules:
    - name: check-signature
      match:
        resources:
          kinds: [Pod]
      verifyImages:
        - imageReferences:
            - "*.gcr.io/tenant-*/**"
          attestors:
            - entries:
                - keyless:
```
